observationsNotFindings: The reserved-device-name prohibition is the one a corpus like this is most likely to trip, because the member is literally called 'reserved device names' and a fixture author will eventually need the list. The file names the class exactly as v6 names it and stops, carrying reservedDeviceNameList NOT-AUTHORED on the one state where the question arises. I verified that by sweeping for CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, CONIN$ and CONOUT$ as whole words rather than by trusting the denial; none appears.

Scope discipline is the other thing worth naming. Live v6's notAuthored object holds five buckets and this corpus takes exactly one. ENVELOPE_MISMATCH sits in the TC-SIG conditional bucket and unicode-norm-duplicate in its own, and both are refused rather than borrowed; the TC-SIG ceremony and TC-ACCEPT multi-component members do not appear at all. A corpus that had quietly widened to the adjacent buckets would have looked like more coverage and been a scope violation.

Windows is deferred from slice 1 by D-002 with explicit disposition, so this corpus names inputs for a platform outside the current slice. That is consistent with OBL-WINDOWS-PATH being leftover-design on DR-103 rather than required-now work, and the subject does not present it as slice-1 coverage. Nothing here changes Windows' deferral.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no SHOULD-FIX. The central check is an exact-set question and it passes three ways: live component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v6 carries notAuthored['Windows-only TC-PATH'] as reserved device names, trailing dot, trailing space, and the subject reproduces that list element-wise at basedOn.corpusV6.windowsOnlyTcPathVerbatim, at the top-level assertsNamedNotAuthored, and as the ordered memberVerbatim values of its three states - one state per member, none invented, none dropped. The prohibition most at risk here is the reserved-device-name list, since the member is literally named for it; I swept for CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, CONIN$ and CONOUT$ as whole words rather than trusting the denial, and found none, with reservedDeviceNameList NOT-AUTHORED on the state where the question arises. Scope discipline also holds: v6's notAuthored object has five buckets and this corpus takes exactly one, refusing ENVELOPE_MISMATCH and unicode-norm-duplicate rather than borrowing them, and never mentioning the TC-SIG ceremony or TC-ACCEPT members. Both refusals match live standing rather than being bare assertions - ENVELOPE_MISMATCH is an INACTIVE conditional RJ-4 subcode pending ID-DEP-1 and ID-DEP-5, and v6 itself records unicode-norm-duplicate as BLOCKED on pathRule / RJ-3 pending a schema successor. 5/5 cited digests recompute, three of them artifacts I pinned independently earlier in this session. Bare integers are 1, 0, 0 and 26, so nothing numeric is smuggled in, and the live OBL-WINDOWS-PATH obligation still reads leftoverDesign true. 14 attacks run, 14 refuted.
